title: News media as suppliers of narratives (and information)
title_zh: 新闻媒体作为叙事（及信息）的提供者
authors: Kfir Eliaz, Ran Spiegler
abstract: We present a model in which news media shape beliefs by providing information (signals about an exogenous state) and narratives (models of what determines outcomes). To amplify consumers' engagement, the media maximize their anticipatory utility. We characterize the optimal monopolistic media strategy, highlighting the synergy between false narratives and biased information. Consumer heterogeneity gives rise to a novel menu‐design problem due to an “equilibrium data externality” among consumers. The optimal menu includes false narratives, and can generate polarized beliefs and choices without any information transmission. False narratives and polarization also feature in a competitive version of our model, albeit coupled with complete information. Nevertheless, competition can make some consumers objectively worse off.

title: Assessing the environmental implications of sustainable public procurement of food
title_zh: 评估可持续公共食品采购的环境影响
authors: Michael Martin, Sofia Lingegård
abstract: Sustainable public procurement (SPP) is increasingly recognized as a policy tool to improve the environmental performance of food systems, yet there is limited empirical evidence on how procurement strategies influence environmental outcomes. This study assesses the environmental implications of municipal food procurement in a rural Swedish region using life cycle assessment (LCA). Procurement data from Östersund Municipality were used to construct baseline and alternative scenarios that reflect policy targets and objectives, including increased sourcing of organic and local foods, substitution of beef with game or legumes, and reductions in plate waste. Environmental impacts were evaluated using the Impact World + method across multiple indicators, including climate change, eutrophication, biodiversity, toxicity, and resource use. The results show that procurement strategies have differing effects across impact categories. Measures targeting food composition and consumption, such as reducing beef consumption and plate waste, lead to consistent reductions across several indicators, whereas strategies focused on sourcing and production methods, such as organic and local, yield more mixed outcomes, with improvements in some categories but increases in others. Substituting minced beef with local game and reducing food waste result in the largest overall reductions, while increasing organic procurement leads to relatively small changes across most indicators. These findings highlight the importance of multi-indicator assessments and show that focusing on a single indicator, or target, risks overlooking trade-offs. The study provides empirical evidence supporting more targeted, evidence-based procurement strategies and highlights the need for improved life cycle inventory data.

title: Bilateral Import Demand Elasticities and Balanced Trade Protection
title_zh: 双边进口需求弹性与平衡贸易保护
authors: Kee, Hiau Looi, Constantinescu, Cristina, Yotov, Yoto V.
source: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
official: 官方在线 2026-06-29 · 来源：出版社网页
abstract: Recognizing that macroeconomic conditions determine aggregate trade imbalances, can tariffs eliminate bilateral trade deficits? The Balanced Trade Tariff Index (BTTI) is introduced as the uniform tariff that closes bilateral deficits while holding macroeconomic conditions fixed. The BTTI depends on bilateral, product-level import demand elasticities estimated using a translog GDP function applied to data from seven major economies. The novel elasticity estimates vary widely across importers, exporters, products, and trade directions. This heterogeneity lowers average implied tariffs relative to homogeneous-elasticity benchmarks, yet implies substantially higher tariffs are required for exporters of inelastic products, underscoring the limits of tariffs for balancing trade.

title: Income Inequality and Job Creation
title_zh: 收入不平等与就业创造
authors: Sebastian Doerr, Thomas Drechsel, Donggyu Lee
abstract: Abstract We propose a novel channel through which rising income inequality affects job creation and macroeconomic outcomes. High-income households save relatively more in stocks and bonds but less in bank deposits. A rising top income share thereby increases the relative financing cost for bank-dependent firms, which in turn create fewer jobs compared to other firms. Exploiting variation in top income shares across US states and an instrumental variable strategy, we provide evidence for this channel. We then build a general equilibrium macroeconomic model with heterogeneous households and heterogeneous firms and calibrate it to our empirical estimates. The model shows that the secular rise in top incomes accounts for 13% of the decline in the employment share of small firms since 1980. Through the new channel, rising inequality also reduces the labor share and aggregate output. Model experiments show that ignoring the link between inequality and job creation understates welfare effects of income redistribution.

title: Public Services Under Private Management
title_zh: 私营管理下的公共服务
authors: MaÍra Coube, Luiz Felipe Fontes, Rudi Rocha
abstract: Abstract Theory predicts that outsourcing public services to the private sector can reduce costs and improve efficiency, but can also induce cost-cutting and compromise quality. We assess the Brazilian “Organizações Sociais de Saude” model (OSS), which outsources management of public hospital services to the private sector while the state remains the residual claimant. We show that this enhances hospital production and operational efficiency without adverse effects on hospital quality and equity. Increased inpatient production addresses previously unmet demand, expanding local access to hospital care and reducing population mortality. Performance gains arise from improved operational efficiency achieved through increased hospital management capacity. This facilitates staffing adjustments, favoring higher-skilled personnel, dismissing lower-productivity staff, and adopting flexible, performance-tied employment contracts. Effects are larger among private organizations with more management experience, underscoring returns to managerial capacity. Our findings show that incentive-ownership structures can address the quantity-quality trade-off in public service delivery, even when contracts are incomplete and quality is hard to measure.
